title: Doctorant(e) - "Vers un bâtiment low-tech : caractériser et réduire les dépendances liées à la maintenance et à l'entretien du bâti face au changement climatique"
description: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain . Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif. L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain. Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol. Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles. ✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables. 🏠 Contexte Présentation du sujet Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023). Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes. En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées. Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation. Contexte scientifique La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique. Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants. La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés. Contexte opérationnel Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer : les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ; les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ; les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ; les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs). Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire. Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire. 🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous Démarche de la thèse L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments. Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS . Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux. Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités). Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs. Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées. Verrous scientifiques : Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux) Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles Objectifs de développement durable rattachés : ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables · ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsables ODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques. 🔍 Ce que nous recherchons Formation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus. title: Infrastructure Engineer (m/f/d) - IT Infrastructure Services
description: At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable. It is your responsibility to identify improvement opportunities, drive identity projects, and build a unified, scalable environment. Based in Germany and the US, our IT Infrastructure Services team designs, implements, and manages global cloud and on-premises infrastructure solutions to provide Flix with internal business services such as identity and access management, security and compliance configuration, communication tools, file sharing, 3rd-level support, and infrastructure consulting. About the Role Integrate new internal and external applications into our identity infrastructure (e.g., SSO ) following best practices Work on projects to improve internal role-based access control concepts Consult other teams and guide them to success, leveraging our services especially regarding identity and access management Drive innovation and improve our services together with the team Automate recurring tasks Design the future IT infrastructure of Flix About You At least 3 years of experience with Microsoft Entra ID or similar identity and access management platforms Advanced knowledge of modern authentication protocols ( OIDC , OAuth 2.0, and SAML ) At least 3 years of scripting experience (ideally with Python) At least 1 year of experience with IaC solutions (preferably Terraform) Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools to streamline infrastructure automation, troubleshooting, and daily operations Basic experience using APIs Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is a plus Experience working with IaaS solutions is a plus Basic knowledge of modern frontend frameworks (e.g., React) or web technologies is a plus Experience with M365 products (such as Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams) is a plus We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. What We Offer Travel perks : 12 free Flix vouchers + 12 discount vouchers for friends & family. Work from (M)Anywhere : Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year. title: Senior Software Engineer (Java/SpringBoot)
description: Atolls is the world's largest community-driven shopping platform, active in 20+ markets. We help millions make smarter spending decisions across discovery, evaluation, and (re-)purchase by connecting people with the right brands and retailers. Our 1,000+ team across 10 countries builds products used every day at global scale, where you'll have real ownership and see your impact. Want to shape the destinations people rely on to shop with confidence? Keep reading. About This Role: We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Java/SpringBoot) to join our Shopping team in Berlin . At Atolls, your role will be instrumental in helping us to let our consumers maximize value for their money by providing a world-class shopping rewards experience online and in-store, creating exceptional user experiences and empowering consumers to make informed and confident shopping decisions. As a key part of our team, you'll be directly involved in building and enhancing the digital destinations our users rely on throughout their shopping journeys. Your contributions will help shape how millions of consumers interact with our platforms, guiding them to make smart, fair, and rewarding choices. Our Benefits: At Atolls, we believe in nurturing both your professional and personal growth. Here's what you can expect: A culture that values personal and professional development, with internal mobility opportunities. A supportive and open-minded team that embraces diverse perspectives and innovative ideas. 32 days of paid vacation plus your birthday off, giving you the time you need to recharge. A flexible hybrid working scheme to balance work and life. Access to a learning budget and internal training to help you grow in your role. Mental health coaching to support your well-being. Regular global and local get-togethers to celebrate successes and build connections. The possibility of taking a sabbatical after three years with the company. A cloud-based company setup, providing flexibility and collaboration opportunities no matter where you are. *These are global benefits that apply to all employees, with additional local perks based on your location. Responsibilities: In this role, you will: Design and develop modern architectures using Java, AWS technologies, microservices, NoSQL & RDBMS, event-driven architectures, etc. Be involved in the inception, development, and delivery of various features and products on an ambitious and challenging product roadmap. Take responsibility for our solution architecture and contribute to improving it in terms of performance, security, scalability, modularity, and operational efficiency. Be involved in multiple projects at the same time and manage your time effectively. Conduct knowledge-sharing sessions through presentations and hands-on tasks that help practice new technologies. Your Profile: We're looking for someone with 6+ years of experience, who is dedicated to creating exceptional user experiences and driving innovation. 6+ years of experience in designing and developing complex modular applications from technical planning to implementation within a client-side framework as well as server-side. Strong knowledge and active hands-on experience of Java and SpringBoot . Object-oriented programming concepts with application to concurrent event-based systems. Previous knowledge and experience with JS (TypeScript, NodeJS), HTML, CSS and React/Angular. Knowledge of AWS technologies such as DynamoDB, Elasticsearch, relational and NoSQL databases, EventBridge and messaging and queuing solutions like SQS, SNS (or any other cloud platform like Google Cloud or Azure). Experience with GraphQL, federation and Supergraph concepts. Excellent understanding of common design/architectural patterns, and the ability to produce elegant designs in modular/microservice design patterns. Logical, analytic thinking, structured and target-oriented approach, very good problem-solving skills. Passion for delivering clean code, unit/integration tests and maintainable documentation. Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies and DevOps best practices. Demonstrated ability to support and mentor more junior members of a software development team. BS degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Excellent communication skills and fluency in written and spoken English. Our hiring process : TA Call : Meet one of our Talent Experts and get to know Atolls better. Technical Round : Focus on the technical aspects of the role (Through a Live Case) , and meet your potential manager. Final Round : Meet other Atollians 🏝️ It varies from 1 to 3 interviews *Some processes might slightly change according to needs Ready to apply? Be part of a destination where your work helps millions of people make better decisions every day. One focused application is all we need. If you truly fit more than one role, you're welcome to apply to up to three. This helps us match you with the right opportunity faster. We review every application with equal care and will reach out if your profile aligns. Apply now with your CV in English. #LI-AK1 At Atolls, we want to ensure that all employees can thrive in an inclusive environment. Our employment opportunities are open to every gender, race, religion, age, sexual orientation, ability, place of origin, or socioeconomic status. We remain committed to a culture of diversity, equity and belonging, where all employees are welcomed, respected, connected, and engaged. As part of our recruitment process at Atolls, we use AI tools for interview recording and transcription. These tools are designed to assist our teams and are never used independently to make hiring decisions. Every assessment and hiring decision is made by our hiring panel and team through human judgment. Before your first interview, you will receive an email with the option to opt out. You can also change your preference at any time during the recruitment process by using the link in that email or by contacting your Talent Acquisition Partner. The use of AI, or the choice not to use it, will not affect your application in any way. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Energy Analyst
description: About us Gridcog is a global SaaS start-up of energy nerds on a mission to accelerate investment in the clean energy transition. We build project modelling software that captures the physical and commercial detail of energy projects, front-of-meter and behind the meter, so our users can make intelligent energy decisions. Our clients have modelled over 17k projects in over 40 markets globally. Germany is one of our most important markets. We've built a strong brand here and work with some of the most active developers, IPPs and energy companies in the country, including MaxSolar, Lintas, Suncatcher, Octopus Energy Generation, TotalEnergies and Shell. Who we're looking for We're looking for a Senior Energy Analyst with deep knowledge of the German power market to join our Berlin office. You'll be the second person in the office and a senior voice for Gridcog in Germany. Your main job is to own our German customer relationships. You'll make sure customers model their projects well, get real value from Gridcog and keep choosing us. You'll use your market knowledge and network to make Gridcog a trusted voice in the market, help win new customers and make sure the product works for the target customer group. What you'll do Customers (the core of the role) Own a portfolio of German customer relationships as their main point of contact and trusted advisor Lead onboarding and guide customers on best practice modelling of solar, BESS and hybrid projects in Germany Handle complex technical and market questions, such as ancillary market participation, grid connection constraints, AgNes, and merchant versus contracted revenues Spot where accounts can grow and work with account management on renewals and expansion Keep our German datasets current, including market prices, network tariffs and project assumptions Sales and marketing Lead demos and technical conversations with prospects, including senior stakeholders, e.g., partners, investment managers, MDs Build Gridcog's credibility in Germany and Central Europe through speaking at events and through your professional network, e.g., on LinkedIn Translate regulatory changes and market design developments into clear insight for customers Create blogs, videos and market commentary on the German market Speak and present at industry events Product Bring German market requirements into product development and make sure they are understood and prioritised Feed market changes into product direction and feature development Test new features against real client use cases What it's like being second in the office Much of how we operate in Germany is still being built, and you'll often be the one setting it up. There won't always be a playbook. You'll need to make calls with incomplete information, act on them and adjust as you learn. We value moving fast over getting everything perfect, and we'd rather you ship something good and improve it than hold it back. To be successful in this role you will have 3 to 10 years' experience in the German power sector, with solid knowledge of market dynamics, regulation and commercial models for utility-scale solar and battery storage A track record of owning client relationships and delivering excellent outcomes for them The confidence and credibility to represent Gridcog externally, lead demos and engage senior stakeholders Comfort working in an unstructured environment, making decisions and learning from what doesn't work Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data An engaging communication style and the motivation to create content and present at events over time A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for working in a growing, international team Fluent German and English, and based in or open to relocating to Berlin We'd also love it if you have Experience in sales or pre-sales, such as demos or client-facing analysis Practical experience in energy project modelling Familiarity with tools such as Excel, Tableau, Python or R Exposure to other European energy markets Benefits Competitive remuneration package aligned with experience and skills A Berlin office with flexible working arrangements A high-performing team that values innovation and creative problem-solving Exposure and influence over markets beyond Germany / Central Europe through our international footprint and global teams Support for ongoing professional and personal development An annual all-company retreat, with recent locations including Bali and Bintan Island Diversity and inclusion We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team at Gridcog. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, as we believe an inclusive environment and diversity of perspective lead to innovation and success. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

infrastructure systems.</p></li><li><p><strong>Technical Depth:</strong> Hands-on background in systems programming (Go,Java, Typescript, Ruby/Rails or similar high-performance languages) with the ability to participate in system design reviews and unblock complex technical paths.</p></li><li><p><strong>Domain & Scale Expertise:</strong> Proven track record of operating high-throughput coding tools to optimize team productivity and workflows.</p></li><li><p>Familiarity with OpenAPI standards, relational databases (e.g., Postgres), and observability suites (Prometheus, Grafana, Kibana).</p></li></ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h3>What Makes Cloudflare Special?</h3> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. That means leading teams of Project Leads, Product Owners, and Field Application Engineers, and reporting directly to the Chief Customer Officer. You are an entrepreneurial leader who thrives on turning complex development roadmaps into tangible, high-quality products while balancing the unique demands of both vehicle-level and grid-scale energy storage safety and performance. Strategic Staffing: Optimize organizational structure and resource allocation across programs to balance capacity, driving throughput and profitability. Department Alignment: Act as the primary interface for C-level management, aligning departmental goals with the overall company strategy and reporting on KPIs. Governance & Process Design: Define and continuously optimize department processes and interfaces to other departments (Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Quality). title: Customer Success Manager
description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. The AI Customer Success function is being built from the ground up, and this role will help define it internationally. As the first Customer Success Manager in this area, you will own the end-to-end post-sale experience for a portfolio of customers that includes some of the world’s most sophisticated cyber threat intelligence teams and investigators, national security agencies, and financial crime teams. Your mandate is not just to manage accounts—you will help establish the playbook, define what success looks like, and drive a product-led growth motion that turns new customers into long-term, expanding partners. The impact you will have: Build and ship a v1 onboarding playbook within the first 30 days—a practical, working version built from early customer engagements that can be iterated as you learn what drives adoption across international customer segments. Use AI to build production CS workflows that pull from ChurnZero, Salesforce, Gong, and product usage telemetry to auto-generate account health summaries and QBR drafts—compressing hours of reporting preparation into minutes so you can spend your time on the work that actually requires human judgment. Define and track adoption benchmarks across the portfolio—hands-on-keyboard usage, consumption rates, and account-specific success metrics—and surface at-risk accounts before renewal decisions are made. Identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play within 60 days by working backwards from expansion targets, focusing on the one or two use cases most likely to drive consumption across the customer base. Run executive business reviews and QBRs with senior stakeholders at government agencies and financial institutions internationally—building the trust and credibility that turns TRM from a vendor into a mission-critical partner. Partner with ADs on expansion plays, co-own NRR targets, and build the structured path to proving value for every customer with an expiring or at-risk contract. Close the feedback loop between customers and Product—synthesize adoption blockers, feature gaps, and new use-case opportunities into prioritized, actionable input that informs the roadmap. Design the CS infrastructure and tooling stack that scales as the product grows—you are building the foundation the next CSM hire will inherit. What we're looking for: Background in cyber or cyber threat intelligence, intelligence agencies, financial crime investigations, or regulatory and compliance environments. 5+ years as an onboarding engineer, customer success manager, deployment strategist, or in another post-sale role with proven ownership of NRR, GRR, and expansion metrics—you have the track record, not just the title. Domain credibility in cyber, national security, or financial crime—you can walk into a room of investigators and earn their trust in the first meeting, not the fifth. Demonstrated zero-to-one builder experience—you have built a CS function, onboarding playbook, or PLG motion from scratch and can point to the specific outcomes it drove. Production AI fluency—you have built real, repeatable AI workflows, not just experiments, that synthesize data from multiple sources into outputs that run consistently and deliver measurable results. You can show the workflow, explain the data logic, and articulate where human judgment stays in the loop. A high level of independence—you set your own agenda, operate without needing constant direction, and ship v1 before you have all the answers. Strong executive presence—you can run a QBR with a senior government stakeholder or financial institution executive and command the room through substance, not just polish. Experience supporting international customers, with the ability to navigate regional, cultural, and time-zone differences. About the Team: This team focuses on TRM’s AI-driven Intel platform, supporting investigators and cyber teams working on complex cases involving cyber threats. This is the first Customer Success hire dedicated to international customers—you will help build the function from the ground up, with high autonomy, direct access to leadership, and meaningful influence on how TRM approaches customer success globally. The broader TRM CS organization operates distributed, not distant—async-first communication through Slack, strong documentation, and intentional synchronous time for key decisions. You will work directly with the Head of Customer Success and Patrick South, CRO, with close day-to-day collaboration with international Sales teams and Product. Team Operating Rhythms: As a globally distributed team, members work across multiple time zones. This role will primarily align its working hours and customer coverage with international markets, with flexibility to collaborate across regions when needed. Our Customer Success team is fully remote, thriving on asynchronous communication and collaboration through Slack channels and detailed documentation. We hold weekly customer syncs, biweekly health syncs, join our associated POD calls, and regularly engage with customers across international markets. As experts in our craft, we focus on providing support, driving value, and building meaningful relationships with our customers as trusted advisors. We are on the front lines of TRM, ensuring our customers get the most out of the product and bringing valuable insights back to the team. The team moves fast and iterates—v1 ships before it is perfect, and feedback is expected to be direct and specific. On-Call Responsibilities: End-to-End Ownership: While there is no formal hourly rotation, you will be the primary lead for your area and responsible for customer success across international markets. This requires a high degree of agency and a commitment to seeing mission-critical tasks through to resolution, including the flexibility to handle urgent needs outside of standard hours or on weekends when they arise. Learn about TRM Speed in this position: Within 30 days of joining, you ship a working v1 onboarding playbook built from your first 2–3 accounts—not a slide deck, but a live document with measurable adoption benchmarks that the account team is already using to set customer expectations. Within 6 weeks, you share a draft success-metrics framework at 50% complete with the account team and key customers to validate direction—getting real signal on what drives credit consumption before investing further in building out the full playbook. Within 60 days, you identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play by working backwards from expansion targets—presenting a concrete recommendation to leadership on which use case to prioritize and why, grounded in actual account data from international customers. title: Field Application Engineer
description: About Us Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world. The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone. Role Summary The Field Application Engineer (FAE) is a hands-on, vehicle system-level role. You will work directly on prototype vehicles and lab cars to investigate complex, cross-subsystem issues, capturing the data needed to reproduce and isolate them. You will also provide diagnostic and integration support on-site at partner facilities. The focus is on getting close to the hardware and the buses, producing clear findings that development teams can act on. This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite, with occasional travel to other company and partner sites as needed. Responsibilities Perform hands-on diagnostics on prototype vehicles, including capturing network traces (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and real-time data logs from ECUs and zonal controllers. Work at the vehicle system level to reproduce, characterize, and isolate reported issues across interacting subsystems. Set up and operate measurement and diagnostic equipment to gather ground-truth data directly from the vehicle. Run first-pass triage of field-reported symptoms to help distinguish software defects from environmental or hardware issues. Reproduce and characterize reported issues on target vehicles and test benches.. Document technical findings, logs, and reproduction steps into clear hand-off reports for development teams. Log and update technical tickets in Jira, keeping status and evidence current.. Travel to customer / partner sites, both domestically and internationally, for on-site diagnostics and integration support. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience. Foundational understanding of automotive network protocols (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and willingness to deepen it quickly. Hands-on experience with bus-monitoring / diagnostic tools (e.g., Vector CANalyzer, PCAN, or equivalent) — required. Basic understanding of embedded systems and embedded operating systems. Scripting/programming ability (Python and/or C/C++) for log processing and data capture. Experience working within a CI/CD environment. Experience working with and developing within git. Comfortable working hands-on with hardware in a lab or vehicle environment.. Fluency in English required. Total Rewards We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. title: Electrical Engineer (Launcher)
description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. Overview Harmattan AI is developing new hardware products within the Launcher module: field-deployable drone launchers designed to be deployed and operated autonomously in demanding field environments. These products require dedicated electronics design with complex architecture in a constrained environment – PCBs integrating power conversion, energy management, control and communication interfaces – optimised for cost at volume. The Launcher team is seeking a dedicated hardware engineer to own electronics design end-to-end and accelerate the path to production milestones. Ideal candidate A senior hardware engineer who has designed and shipped complex PCBs, ideally mixing digital and significant power (hundreds of watts), into production. They are rigorous on schematics, layout, and bring-up, and have a strong instinct for cost and manufacturability. They design with real-world operating conditions in mind - temperature, moisture, surges - and an interest in battery thermal management; direct experience of outdoor-deployed equipment is a plus rather than a prerequisite. They are comfortable working autonomously in a small team and can bridge hardware and firmware. Skills required PCB schematic and layout design (Altium Designer preferred) Power electronics design: ~300 W DC/DC conversion, protection, derating, efficiency and thermal budgets Thermal regulation: temperature sensing and control loops, battery storage temperature management, heatsinking Power over Ethernet (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt): combined power and data delivery, isolation, cable budgets Mixed-signal design: power management, MCU interfaces, communication buses (SPI, I2C, UART, USB, CAN, Ethernet) Hardware bring-up and debug: bench equipment proficiency DFM/DFA for PCB manufacturing and assembly Component selection and BOM management Experience in lightning and surge protection is a plus Responsibilities: Schematic Design - Design complete schematics for mixed-signal and power boards, from power stages to digital and communication sections. PCB Layout & Routing - Perform or lead board placement and routing with attention to signal integrity, EMC, and power-path constraints. Power & Thermal Architecture - Define and validate the power architecture of the product and the thermal strategy, including battery temperature management. Environmental Robustness - Ensure the electronics withstand outdoor deployment conditions and define the associated qualification plan. Component Selection & BOM Optimization - Select components with cost, availability, and reliability in mind; drive BOM cost reduction for mass production volumes. Hardware Bring-up & Debug - Lead board bring-up, debug issues with oscilloscopes, power bench equipment, and other bench equipment; write bring-up scripts when needed. EMC & Safety Compliance - Address EMC challenges; ensure signal integrity across the board and electrical safety of the power and battery sections. Collaboration with Embedded SW - Work closely with the embedded software engineer to define hardware/software interfaces; support firmware bring-up. Collaboration with Mechanical - Ensure seamless PCB integration into mechanical enclosures (connectors, mounting, thermal, sealing, shielding). Supplier & Manufacturing Ramp-up - Qualify PCB manufacturers and assembly houses; support DFM/DFA review for production; manage NPI transitions. Documentation - Maintain schematics, layout files, test procedures, and hardware specifications. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement. Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply. What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator. What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. Conditions Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

You know where work gets stuck because you've lived it.</li> <li>Comfort building with AI tools: agents, skills, prompt engineering, MCP integrations, no-code/low-code platforms. </li> <li>A product management mindset: you think in terms of intake, backlog, iteration, adoption, and measurable outcomes.</li> <li>Strong communication and the credibility to tell senior stakeholders "not yet" on low-priority requests and "think bigger" when teams default to automating the status quo.</li> <li>Exceptional executive communication and writing skills — clear, concise, transparent, and insightful for teams, executives, and a diverse set of stakeholders.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><h3>What Makes Cloudflare Special?</h3> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. title: Senior Incident Responder (m/w/d)
description: Wir - die HvS-Consulting GmbH – sind Spezialisten für Cyber Security und davon überzeugt, dass die Werte unserer Gesellschaft auch im Cyber-Raum geschützt werden müssen. Deshalb helfen wir Organisationen, sich mit dem richtigen Zusammenspiel aus Technologien, Prozessen und Menschen selbst zu schützen. Unser Motto lautet „People – Process – Technology" Für unser Team in Garching bei München suchen wir ab sofort eine(n) Senior Incident Responder (m/w/d) Aufgaben Das erwartet Dich: Incident Response : Du betreust komplexe Cyber Security Incidents bei unseren Kunden und begleitest die First Response, Analyse, Eindämmung, Aufarbeitung und Wiederherstellung Incident-Leitung : Du steuerst Sicherheitsvorfälle, koordinierst alle beteiligten Parteien und sorgst für eine strukturierte, zielorientierte und verlässliche Bearbeitung. Dabei bildest Du die Schnittstelle zwischen den technischen Workstreams und der Entscheider-Ebene, beispielsweise dem Krisenstab oder dem Management. Du kommunizierst sicher mit technischen Ansprechpartnern sowie dem Management und steuerst das Incident Response Team Security Consulting : Du berätst unsere Kunden vor und nach Sicherheitsvorfällen ganzheitlich, um die Strategie, die technische Architektur, Prozesse und Skills des Cyber Defense Centers weiterzuentwickeln Threat Landscape : Gemeinsam mit deinem Team behältst Du die aktuelle Bedrohungslage im Blick. Du informierst unsere Kunden auf technischer und Management-Ebene über relevante Bedrohungen und gibst konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen Technische Schulungen : Du konzipierst und hältst Schulungen, Workshops, Trainings und Übungen rund um Incident Response, Digitaler Forensik und CDC Service Management : Du verantwortest die Qualität und Weiterentwicklung unserer Incident-Response-Services und setzt neue Ideen konsequent um Konzepte und Prozesse: Du entwickelst unsere Incident-Response-Konzepte, Prozesse und Standards kontinuierlich weiter und etablierst praxistaugliche Strukturen Qualifikation Das bringst Du mit: Führungserfahrung : Du bringst mehrjährige Führungserfahrung mit und hast bereits ein Team fachlich und disziplinarisch geleitet Incident Response : Du verfügst über fundierte praktische Erfahrung in der Bearbeitung und Koordination komplexer Cyber Security Incidents Threat Landscape : Du kennst die aktuelle Bedrohungslage und verstehst relevante Threat Actors, Angreifertechniken und Angriffsmuster, beispielsweise bei APT-Angriffen, Ransomware, Innentätern oder Supply-Chain-Angriffen Technische Expertise : Du hast Erfahrung im Umgang mit Security-Technologien wie SIEM, EDR und NDR Consulting-Erfahrung : Du bist mit der Beratung von Kunden vertraut und vermittelst technische Sachverhalte klar und adressatengerecht und agierst sicher als Schnittstelle zwischen technischen Workstreams, Krisenstab und Management Schulungserfahrung : Du hast Erfahrung in der Konzeption und Durchführung technischer Schulungen, Workshops oder Übungen Prozesse und Services : Du hast Security-Incident-Management-Prozesse, fachliche Konzepte oder Cyber Security Services entwickelt und erfolgreich weitergeführt KI und Innovation : Du hast Erfahrung in der Integration von KI oder Large Language Models in DFIR-Services oder vergleichbare Tätigkeiten Service Management : Du weißt, wie professionelle Cyber Security Services gesteuert, bewertet und weiterentwickelt werden. Ebenfalls hast Du bereits die potentiale von KI/LLM erkannt und hast diese in Cyber Security Services oder Tätigkeiten integriert Führungspersönlichkeit : Du führst klar und verbindlich, kannst Menschen motivieren und gehst empathisch auf unterschiedliche Persönlichkeiten ein Gestaltungswille : Du bringst neue Ideen und strategischen Weitblick ein, übernimmst Verantwortung und setzt Veränderungen konsequent um Qualifikation : Du verfügst über ein abgeschlossenes Studium oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung, sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse und rund 20 Prozent Reisebereitschaft (DACH-Raum) Benefits Was dich aber vor allem erwartet: Ein abwechslungsreicher und vielseitiger Job in einem der (aus unserer Sicht) spannendsten Themengebiete überhaupt. Und das in einem Unternehmen, in dem wirklich jede Meinung gehört und geschätzt wird – vom Praktikanten bis zur Geschäftsführung. Uns gibt dieser Job nicht nur ein Gehalt, sondern auch persönliche Zufriedenheit, weil wir wirklich etwas bewirken und die Welt ein Stück sicherer machen. Bei uns gibt es (natürlich) kostenlose Getränke, Kaffee und Snacks, aber das ist heutzutage Standard. Zusätzlich bieten wir auf Wunsch attraktive Benefits, von Jobticket bis hin zu Kindergartenzuschuss. Flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten helfen Dir, auch auf Unvorhergesehenes im Alltag gelassen zu reagieren. Schau dir unsere Benefits gerne auf unserer Karriereseite genauer an. Was erwartet Dich noch? Wir pflegen eine offene, vertrauensvolle Unternehmenskultur (schau mal auf Kununu ) und schätzen eigenständiges Arbeiten, natürlich auch, aber nicht nur im Home-Office. Schließlich haben wir ein modernes Büro in Garching mit sensationellem Alpenblick, in dem wir gerne gemeinsam Mittagsessen und uns mit unseren Security-Auditoren, Incident-Respondern, Awareness-Trainern und Multimedia-Designern austauschen. title: Head of GTM, AI Inference
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3>About Us</h3> <p>At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><h2>Available Locations</h2> <ul> <li>New York, US</li> <li>San Francisco, US</li> </ul> <h2>About the Role</h2> <p data-path-to-node="4">Cloudflare is building one of the most differentiated AI inference platforms in the market. We aren’t building another commoditized GPU-by-the-hour provider, but a globally distributed, serverless inference platform integrated into the world's largest developer ecosystem. We are looking for a leader to partner across our organization and own the go-to-market strategy for this business.</p> <p data-path-to-node="5">As Head of GTM, AI Inference, you will serve as key connective tissue between our cutting-edge AI infrastructure, our product teams, and the global market. You will work directly with Workers AI prospects evaluating Cloudflare as a source of GPU capacity, partner with product leadership to shape how we position and package our inference capabilities, and build the analytical frameworks that help us target the right strategic customers and partners.</p> <p data-path-to-node="6">In this role, you will help craft our operational playbook, test it against real market signals, and iterate as the landscape shifts. You will bring equal comfort building financial models for inference unit economics and engaging in strategic, consultative conversations with technical leaders and CTOs.</p> <h2>Responsibilities</h2> <h3>Market Strategy & Positioning</h3> <ul> <li> <p data-path-to-node="9,0,0">Lead Cloudflare's GTM strategy for AI inference, defining how we compete beyond the commoditized GPU/hour model.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="9,1,0">Develop and continuously refine our positioning around Cloudflare's structural advantages: serverless GPU pricing, edge-distributed infrastructure, and integration with the broader developer platform (Workers, R2, D1, Agents SDK).</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="9,2,0">Identify and evaluate customer and partner segments where Cloudflare's inference model creates disproportionate value, prioritizing focus areas for maximum impact.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="9,3,0">Guide promotional strategies with key model partners to accelerate the adoption of new models and inference capacity.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Strategic Sales & Revenue</h3> <ul> <li> <p data-path-to-node="11,0,0">Partner directly with Workers AI prospects and high-value accounts evaluating Cloudflare for GPU capacity and inference workloads.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="11,1,0">Lead strategic sales conversations, helping prospects understand the architectural and economic advantages of our approach.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="11,2,0">Collaborate with Sales and Developer GTM leadership to build repeatable qualification frameworks and deal structures for inference revenue.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Market Intelligence & Cross-Functional Leadership</h3> <ul> <li> <p data-path-to-node="13,0,0">Serve as Cloudflare's primary listener and synthesizer for inference market signals: pricing shifts, competitive moves, model ecosystem changes, and emerging workload patterns.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="13,1,0">Facilitate internal alignment across Product, Strategy, Engineering, and GTM leadership to translate market intelligence into clear product and commercial decisions.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="13,2,0">Partner with the AI Gateway / Models Marketplace team to align strategy across both the hosting and consumption sides of the model ecosystem—ensuring our GTM motion is coherent across all channels.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Analytics & Business Rigor</h3> <ul> <li> <p data-path-to-node="15,0,0">Build the analytical foundations for the inference business: unit economics models, customer segmentation frameworks, win/loss analysis, and pipeline forecasting.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="15,1,0">Define and track meaningful business metrics for an inference platform at our stage—focusing on sustainable growth, product-market fit, and revenue quality.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="15,2,0">Utilize data-informed insights to guide strategy, test hypotheses, and adapt approach as market dynamics evolve.</p> </li> </ul> <h2>Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience</h2> <p>At Cloudflare, we know that great candidates come from diverse backgrounds with non-linear paths. You don’t need to tick every single box to be right for this role. If you are excited about building a better Internet and ready to make an impact, please apply.</p> <ul> <li> <p data-path-to-node="17,0,0"><strong data-path-to-node="17,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">GTM & Domain Experience:</strong> Demonstrated leadership in GTM strategy, revenue growth, or strategic sales within AI infrastructure, cloud compute, or developer platforms.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="17,1,0"><strong data-path-to-node="17,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">AI Ecosystem Knowledge:</strong> Solid understanding of the AI inference landscape, including model serving economics, GPU capacity dynamics, and ecosystem players.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="17,2,0"><strong data-path-to-node="17,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Analytical Aptitude:</strong> Ability to prospective partners.</p> </li> <li> <p data-path-to-node="17,4,0"><strong data-path-to-node="17,4,0" data-index-in-node="0">Adaptability:</strong> Comfort navigating fast-evolving markets, making title: Applied AI Engineer, Startups (Codex)
description: About the team The Applied AI Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior. This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows. Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work. In this role, you will: Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software. Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption. Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability. Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform. Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value. Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. You’ll thrive in this role if you: Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved. Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools.
